ios.desc:
AIpine [ai·pine] is the pocket toolkit for AI-generated files.

AI tools now create more than text. They generate React components, Mermaid diagrams, CSV exports, SQL scripts, Markdown docs, SVG icons, JSON data, and more. But downloaded to your phone, that output usually ends up as raw files with no good way to view, inspect, or reuse it.

AIpine gives those artifacts a home.

Import files from the Files app or share sheet, then open them the way they were meant to be seen. Preview the result, inspect the source, organize your library, and keep your best AI outputs close at hand.

Render and preview:
• JSX: live React 18 interactions, fully offline
• HTML: rendered web previews
• Mermaid: flowcharts and diagrams
• SVG: centered vector previews with dark mode support
• Markdown: clean, readable documents
• CSV and TSV: scrollable tables with full cell inspection
• JSON, YAML, TOML, SQL, Python, Shell, TypeScript, and JavaScript: syntax-highlighted source with line numbers

Switch between preview and source when you want to see both the finished artifact and the code behind it. Customize code themes, search inside files, mark favorites, reopen recent artifacts, filter by type, and sort your library in seconds.

Like a compact pocket tool for AI work, AIpine keeps the viewers you need in one place, ready whenever an AI assistant gives you something worth saving.

Works with artifacts from Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Codex, and other tools that generate text-based output.

No account. No server. No cloud. Your files stay in your Documents folder on your device.

quotes.text:
I frequently make use of Claude, along with other AI programs, to create various artifacts, such as a component in one session, a Python script in another session, Mermaid diagrams, and Markdown files. The constant issue was that I just couldn’t find any of the artifacts once they were done since all they would do is end up in my chat history.

That’s why I developed AIpine (ai-pine): a Swiss Army knife for AI artifacts, based precisely on this kind of problem.

AIpine is an iOS native viewer supporting the formats that AI tools generate: JSX, Python, HTML, Markdown, Mermaid, CSV, and others. It allows viewing the generated code with a live preview when available, organizing and searching through the artifacts and the possibility of searching through the code directly so that finding “that thing I made three weeks ago” becomes feasible.

It has been out in the App Store for some time now, and I continue developing new functionality. If you work a lot with Claude or other AI tools and create lots of artifacts, I would be very happy to hear from you what format or workflow I could add to help you even more.

It is a $0.99 one-time purchase, with no data collected: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6775947157
